items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'what if' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how cool this story is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement ('WOW' energy), build excitement through each line, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. 'Plot twist' / 'Twist ये है' gets a playful, knowing, excited lift. 'But that's not even the weirdest part' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. The 1903 canal story is told like a thrilling heist. The last line trails off unfinished, voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Pronounce Darién as dah-ree-EN and Bogotá as boh-goh-TAH.
lines: What if Colombia and Panama became one country?
For over eighty years, Panama belonged to Colombia.
So in nineteen-oh-three, Panama broke away... with US warships watching.
Two weeks later, America got its canal deal.
The canal opened in nineteen fourteen... in Panama, not Colombia.
So what would this country get today?
Fifty-eight million people... two oceans... and the Panama Canal.
An economy bigger than Norway's or Singapore's.
But that's not even the weirdest part.
There's no road between them. None.
Just about a hundred kilometers of jungle: the Darién Gap.
The only break in a highway from Alaska to Argentina.
Then there's the capital. Bogotá... or Panama City?
And Colombia's one demand? The coffee stays Colombian.
So... one country, or two? Because honestly...
